newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: YACHTSMEN IN REMARKABLY GOOD MEDICAL CONDITION
Doctors at Fremantle Hospital treating rescued around-the-world yachtsmen, Tony Bullimore and Thierry Dubois, say they have coped with their ordeals remarkably well.
The two sailors, who were rescued by the Australian Defence Forces after their yachts capsized in the Southern Ocean about 14-hundred nautical miles south west of Perth, arrived in Fremantle today.
Thousands of people turned out to welcome navy frigate, HMAS Adelaide, which plucked the men from the freezing waters last week.
Fremantle Hospital's Director of Hypobaric Medicine, Harry Oxer, says Mr Dubois is suffering only from a sore thumb.
Dr Oxer says Mr Bullimore has frostbite on his fingers and toes.
He'll be treated daily in the hospital's decompression chamber, but won't have to remain in hospital overnight and should make a full recovery.
Dr Oxer says neither yachtsman appears to be suffering from shock.
Mr Bullimore's expected to be reunited with his wife at the hospital later this afternoon.
SAILOR THANKS TIM FISCHER OVER AN AUSSIE WINE
French sailor Rafael Dinelli has thanked Acting Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, for his rescue.
Mr Dinelli, the first of three yachtsmen saved, is visiting Canberra to thank the authorities involved in his rescue.
He and Mr Fischer have shared some Australian wine together.
Mr Fischer says the recue of the three round-the world yachtsmen is one of those moments when Australia can feel justifiably proud.
ASSAULT ACCUSED BAILED UNTIL NEXT MONTH
In Queensland, two people charged with the assault of three Vietnamese people on the Gold Coast last week have been bailed to reappear in Court next month.
It's alleged the three members of the one family were kicked and beaten in front of a Surfers Paradise Service station last Monday evening

Twenty-four year old Nicole Louise McConnell and 23 year old Ryan Anthonie Ells entered no plea in the Southport Magistrate's Court today to three counts of assault causing bodily harm, and one of stealing.
The hearing was adjourned until February 11.
SUSPECTS SOUGHT IN KILLING OF GEELONG PENSIONER
Police are appealing for public help to find the suspects in the murder of an elderly Geelong woman.
Seventy-five year old Edna Findlay died after being assaulted with a blunt weapon on Sunday morning.
The house was then set alight and the frail woman had little chance of escape.
Police say the woman owned a number rental properties in the West Geelong area.
Inspector Paul Sheridan of the Homicide Squad says police want to speak to any current or past tenants to help in the investigation.
ERA SAYS NO TAILINGS CRISIS AT RANGER MINE
Mining company ERA has denied claims that miners are working around the clock to contain water levels in the tailings dam at its Ranger uranium mine.
The Northern Territory Environment Centre made the claim about the mine, situated in Kakadu National Park.
ERA chief executive officer, Phillip Shirvington, says tailings water is being transferred into a pit at the site.
Mr Shirvington says company decided a number of years ago to develop the pit in order to hold excess tailings water.
MORE VOICES TO BE ADDED TO EUTHANASIA DEBATE
Northern Territorians wanting to have their say in the euthanasia debate will get their chance next week.
The Senate Committee on Legal and Constitutional Legislation will sit in Darwin, with a public forum on the Territory's voluntary euthanasia law planned for next Thursday.
Hearings before the committee of six permanent and several participatory members, will then take place on the Friday.
The committee will report to the Senate, before it votes on the Andrews bill, aimed at over-turning the Territory's legislation.
FROMBERG HAPPY WITH FITNESS
In tennis, Australia's Richard Fromberg says he's happy with his fitness after winning a five set first round match at the Australian Open today.
Fromberg beat New Zealander, Brett Steven, 4-6, 2-6, 7-5, 6-3, 6-1 to join countryman, Todd Woodbridge, in the second round.
Fromberg says he's worked very hard for the Open and was pleased to win after a disappointing performance in Adelaide at the Australian Hardcourt Championships last week.
Of the other Australians in action today, Toby Mitchell lost to Spain's Alex Corretja, and Evie Dominikovic lost to Latvia's Larisa Neiland.
ELWOOD THROUGH TO SECOND ROUND OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN
Australia's Annabell Elwood is the first Australian woman through to the second round of the Australian Open at Melbourne Park.
Elwood beat Lori McNeil of the United States, 6-3, 6-2.
Earlier, Todd Woodbridge and Richard Fromberg became the first Aussies through to round two.
Others through today include number two seed, Michael Chang, former Wimbledon Champion, Michael Stich, and number seven seed, Thomas Enqvist.
